pointers.sentence: A handler never makes a plain `HttpRequest`: it makes a `WSGIRequest` or an `ASGIRequest`, a subclass that knows how to fill those attributes from what its kind of server passes (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest`, `django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest`, `django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest`).

A handler never makes a plain `HttpRequest`: it makes a `WSGIRequest` or an `ASGIRequest`, a subclass that knows how to fill those attributes from what its kind of server passes (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest`, `django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest`, `django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest`).
The ones a `WSGIRequest` or an `ASGIRequest` makes are immutable, and refuse an assignment ([`QueryDict`](http/querydict.md)) (`django/http/request.py:QueryDict`).

Every other response class is a subclass of one of these two: the redirects, `JsonResponse` and the classes named for a status code are subclasses of `HttpResponse`, and `FileResponse` of `StreamingHttpResponse` ([The response object](http/response.md)) (`django/http/response.py:HttpResponseBase`).

The query string was parsed with the request's encoding, `None` here, which means the default charset, and the form with UTF-8, the one encoding an ordinary form is read in ([`QueryDict`](http/querydict.md)) (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.GET`, `django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._load_post_and_files`).

The query string was parsed with the request's encoding, `None` here, which means the default charset, and the form with UTF-8, the one encoding an ordinary form is read in ([`QueryDict`](http/querydict.md)) (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.GET`, `django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._load_post_and_files`).

A view may read `body`, read the stream itself as a file, or read `POST` and `FILES`, and some of these can follow one another and some cannot ([The body: `body`, `POST` and `FILES`](http/body.md)) (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._load_post_and_files`, `django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.body`).

A view may read `body`, read the stream itself as a file, or read `POST` and `FILES`, and some of these can follow one another and some cannot ([The body: `body`, `POST` and `FILES`](http/body.md)) (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._load_post_and_files`, `django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.body`).

`MultiPartParser` takes the body from the stream in pieces ([Multipart parsing: `MultiPartParser`](http/multipart.md)) and hands a file's pieces to a chain of **upload handlers**, which decide where the file goes; the two installed by default keep the files of a small request in memory and write those of a large one to temporary files on disk ([Upload handlers and uploaded files](http/uploads.md)) (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`, `django/core/files/uploadhandler.py:MemoryFileUploadHandler.handle_raw_input`).

`MultiPartParser` takes the body from the stream in pieces ([Multipart parsing: `MultiPartParser`](http/multipart.md)) and hands a file's pieces to a chain of **upload handlers**, which decide where the file goes; the two installed by default keep the files of a small request in memory and write those of a large one to temporary files on disk ([Upload handlers and uploaded files](http/uploads.md)) (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`, `django/core/files/uploadhandler.py:MemoryFileUploadHandler.handle_raw_input`).

A request over a limit raises a `SuspiciousOperation` at the moment the offending part is read, which may be deep inside a view, and raised inside the middleware chain the exception ordinarily becomes a 400 response at the nearest boundary ([The body: `body`, `POST` and `FILES`](http/body.md#the-limits)) (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).
The cookie was not a header until the handler built the header list: it is kept in `HttpResponseBase.cookies` ([Cookies](http/cookies.md)) (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`).
Under ASGI the handler sends the response itself, as messages, and ordinarily closes it itself ([The two entry points](handlers/entry.md)) (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIHandler.handle`).

The server's `close` is the last call: `HttpResponseBase.close` ends the request ([The two entry points](handlers/entry.md#who-ends-the-request)), and closes the request's uploaded files with it ([Streaming and file responses](http/streaming.md#closing)) (`django/http/response.py:HttpResponseBase.close`).
